text:
nightly-bot: [ALERT] nightly-eval fail: model v3.4.0-int4 on promptset docs-codegen shows regression. pass_rate: 72% -> 44%, avg_ppl +18%. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/2298456000 :warning:
Elena M: ugh, saw this first thing. lots of truncated code blocks and weird token splits in the samples. attaching a diff in a sec.
Carlos (eval): sample IDs 412, 419, 422 show consistent early-stop at 32 tokens. generations look fine on v3.3.9.
Omar S: are we sure this is weight-only? any tokenizer changes in the onboarding branch?
Jing Q: we shipped a tokenizer normalization tweak in v3.4.0 (NFKC + extra byte cleanup) and an int4 weight build. both landed the same week.
Elena M: I compared tokenizations: v3.3.9 -> 68 tokens, v3.4.0 -> 70 tokens (for the same prompt). new tokenizer is inserting a PAD-like U+E000 marker for some sequences.
Carlos (eval): here's a snippet of the failing generation (v3.4.0):
```
<model out> def parse_items(items):\n    if not items:\n        return []\n    for i in items:\n        # truncated here...
```
vs v3.3.9 full output continues.
Maya (infra): any serving-side changes? KV cache handling? we didn't touch runtime this cycle.
Omar S: runtime unchanged, but int4 kernels updated in the docker image tag v3.4.0-int4. could be a KV alignment issue with the new tokenizer causing early eos detection.
Jing Q: running a quick compare of token ids across versions now. command: `python -m tools.token_diff --models v3.3.9 v3.4.0 --promptset docs-codegen --sample 412`
Elena M: results: token ids diverge at position 12 onwards. the new tokenizer emits an extra token that looks like a normalization residue.
Carlos (eval): interestingly, float16 v3.4.0 doesn't show the truncation — suggests quantization interacts with this shift.
Jing Q: probable hypothesis: tokenizer change -> different token boundaries -> KV indexing shift -> int4 optimized kernel misreads cache leading to early termination.
Omar S: repro plan: 1) run single-replica float16 v3.4.0 (no int4) on same hardware 2) run int4 with v3.3.9 tokenizer (force old vocab) 3) run int4 with v3.4.0 tokenizer.
Maya (infra): I'll spin a canary pool with v3.3.9 tokenizer + int4 kernel to see if quantized weights alone are OK. ETA 25m.
Elena M: I pushed a minimal test harness to gh: https://git.redwood/eng/ml/tokenizer-kv-repro. includes scripts and the sample prompts.
Carlos (eval): adding a quick eval compare cmd to CI: `./eval_runner --models v3.3.9,v3.4.0 --quant int4,float16 --promptset docs-codegen --report quick`
Jing Q: early results: forcing v3.3.9 tokenizer with v3.4.0-int4 reduces truncation to baseline. confirms tokenizer is primary vector.
Omar S: mitigation: rollback tokenizer change in the v3.4.1 build (keep int4 kernels) and run new nightly. also add a tokenization hash check in the onboarding job so token counts are compared to baseline automatically.
Elena M: agreed. also add a gating eval that fails the build if token count delta > 2 for docs-codegen anchor prompts.
Maya (infra): canary pool up with forced-old-tokenizer-int4: https://canary.redwood/pools/729 (running tests now).
Carlos (eval): logging looks cleaner already on canary, preliminary pass_rate 69% after forced rollback. still a little variance but within noise.
Jing Q: next actions I will: 1) prepare v3.4.1 with tokenizer rollback 2) run full quantized reproduction matrix 3) write a unit test for normalization edge-case.
Omar S: I'll prepare a rollback+hotfix plan for dedicated customers and add a note to the release notes about tokenizer normalization being opt-in.
Elena M: thanks team. tagging @product to delay rollout until we confirm. :thumbsup:
nightly-bot: noted. will suppress alerts for this model until v3.4.1 is in canary.
Elena M: will post a short postmortem in #eng-ml once we ship fix.
Carlos (eval): saving the failing sample outputs to S3: s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/2298456000/ (files: sample412_v340.json, sample412_v339.json).
Jing Q: I'll follow up with a PR for the tokenizer tests.
Omar S: good triage.
Elena M: closing thread when v3.4.1 passes nightly.
